title: Controls, Monitoring and Kill-Switches
summary: The control environment for agents that act: pre-deployment testing, guardrails, real-time monitoring, human intervention and the ability to stop an agent quickly.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The control environment for agents that act: pre-deployment testing, guardrails, real-time monitoring, human intervention and the ability to stop an agent quickly.
Learning Objectives: Design layered controls and guardrails for agentic systems
Specify monitoring, logging and alerting for agent behaviour
Implement and test kill-switches and human override
Syllabus: Guardrails, hard limits and tool restrictions
Real-time monitoring, audit trails and anomaly detection
Intended Audience: Product, digital, technology and innovation leads designing or deploying AI agents
Compliance, risk, financial crime and legal professionals overseeing agentic AI
Senior managers and directors accountable for AI strategy and its outcomes
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with AI, payments or digital products in a regulated firm is helpful. No technical background in AI is required.
Core Reading: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019, revised 2024)
NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (2023)
FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (2024)
